body.statement: Under the independent Gaussian sampling design, uniformly over \(\theta\in\Theta_K\), \(\Pr_{\theta}[\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}\text{ and }h(\theta)\in\mathcal H_n]\ge1-\alpha\).  The region \(R_n\cap\Theta_K\) is nonempty for every sample, and a rule reports a classification only when \(\mathcal H_n\) is a singleton has probability at most \(\alpha\) of reporting a classification different from \(h(\theta)\).
body.justification: Family coverage must retain structural uncertainty and remain well-defined when the raw covariance region misses the nonclosed model.
body.gap: Strieder et al. retain graph uncertainty by test inversion and Romano--Shaikh cover identified sets, but neither gives always-nonempty coverage of a discontinuous discrete target family under exact-rank covariance restrictions.
body.consumer: A Perturb-seq or Sci-Plex audit can abstain near collisions while maintaining finite-sample coverage of all effective target explanations under the stated covariance model.
